title: Span Compositor: Interactive Multi-Span Comparison Slate
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design an interactive ‘Span Compositor’ slate in the Redwood Console request drill-down that lets engineers compare span-level timing, metadata, and annotations across multiple requests and services. The component should support selecting up to four spans from different traces, time-syncing them, and surfacing KV-cache hits, batching boundaries, and correlation IDs so operators can quickly diagnose variance and regressions in token-level latency.

Scope: UX for span selection and pinning, time-synced scrubber, overlay heatmap for expensive op hotspots, compact span detail panel (metadata, tags, logs link), filters for correlation IDs / service / host / model variant, and an export snapshot action for attaching to incident timelines. Include a prototype for both desktop and tablet breakpoints.

Constraints & non-goals: Not responsible for backend aggregation endpoints (ENG will build /aggregator v2). Design must be frugal with DOM complexity (virtualized span list) and avoid heavy animation that harms frame rate on large traces. We will not implement live streaming updates in first iteration; the slate will refresh on navigation or explicit refresh action.

Acceptance criteria in this ticket below must be met for UX sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Users can select and pin up to 4 spans from any open trace for side-by-side comparison
Time-synced scrubber aligns span timelines and shows relative delta markers
Overlay heatmap highlights high-duration op ranges and KV-cache hit boundaries
Filters available for correlation ID, service, host, and model variant; filters persist across navigation within the session
Compact span panel shows span name, duration, tags, logs link, and associated GitHub trace-id link
Performance: initial render for traces with up to 250 spans should complete under 350ms on mid-tier hardware (target), based on ENG profiling
Snapshot export creates a permalink + JSON bundle suitable for attaching to an incident ticket
decisions_made: Limit pinned spans to 4 to balance screen density and cognitive load
Use time-synced scrubber instead of auto-playback to give operators precise control
Heatmap will be computed server-side as a summary band to minimize client CPU work
Compact span panel is a single-column drawer to maintain vertical rhythm and avoid occluding timeline
